# stems command-line reference

<!-- Generated by `make docs` (`stems __docs`) from the clap definitions in
crates/stems-cli/src/cli.rs. Do not edit by hand: crates/stems-cli/tests/docs.rs
fails when this file drifts; `UPDATE_DOCS=1 cargo test -p stems-cli --test docs`
rewrites it. -->

Every command accepts the global flags shown under `stems`. Output is
human text on a terminal and the JSON envelope
`{ "ok": bool, "data": ..., "errors": [...], "version": "x.y.z" }`
when stdout is not a terminal or with `--json` (`--human` forces text).
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 runtime failure, 2 config/validation/usage error,
3 partial success or orphans, 4 daemon unavailable. Commands whose
deliverable has not landed yet return `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (exit 1).

**Exception:** `stems events --json` prints NDJSON, one event object per
line (`{ts, seq, kind, stem, from, to, reason, actor, data}`) and no
envelope, so external automation can consume `stems events -f --json`
line by line (FR-CL-4); errors (e.g. exit 4 `DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING`) still
print the envelope. The daemon's wire protocol is documented in
`docs/protocol.md`.

## `stems`

```text
Local environment management toolkit for multi-process systems.

stems reads an integration repo's `stems.yaml`, validates it, starts, supervises and tears down
every stem it declares.

Output: human text on a terminal, a JSON envelope `{ "ok", "data", "errors", "version" }` when
stdout is not a terminal or with `--json`. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 runtime failure, 2 config, validation
or usage error, 3 partial success or orphans, 4 daemon unavailable.

Usage: stems [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Lifecycle:
  up             Start stems (and their dependencies), attached or detached
  down           Stop stems in reverse dependency order
  start          Start stems (and unstarted hard dependencies)
  stop           Stop stems
  restart        Restart stems (stop, then start)
  build          Run build scripts (or docker builds)
  pull           Pull the images of docker stems now (a moved tag such as `latest` included)
  watch          Pause or resume watchdogs

Inspect:
  status         Show the state of every stem
  logs           Show or follow stem and script logs
  events         Show or follow the event stream (NDJSON with --json)
  metrics        Show CPU, memory and disk usage per stem
  health         Show the last health probe results per stem, with latency
  graph          Draw the dependency graph

Scripts & context:
  run            Run a stem or workspace script
  scripts        List scripts
  exec           Run an ad-hoc command in a stem's context (env, cwd or container)
  shell          Open an interactive shell in a stem's context
  compose        Run `docker compose` in a compose stem's context (file, project, env)
  reset          Run a stem's `reset` script and clear its stamps
  stamps         Show or clear setup/seed stamps
  overlays       Show the overlays stems has written into codebases, or render a stem's overlays now
                 (`stems overlays render <stem>`)

Config:
  init           Scaffold a new integration repo in the current (or --workspace) directory
  validate       Check the workspace config without starting anything
  show           Print the resolved workspace config (or one stem's)
  switch         Switch a stem to one of its variants (e.g. from a local process to a docker
                 container), or back to `local`
  configuration  List, select or save named configurations (overlays declared under
                 `configurations:` in stems.yaml)
  profiles       List profiles
  config         Read or change local config overrides
  add            Add a stem to stems.yaml
  remove         Remove a stem from stems.yaml
  edit           Open $EDITOR at a stem's block in stems.yaml

Environment & ports:
  env            Print the environment stems gives a stem
  ports          List every stem's host ports and the variables that address them
  outputs        Show values published by stems' `outputs:`

Doctor & repos:
  doctor         Diagnose the environment: Docker, tool versions, ports, orphans
  repos          Clone, update or check out git codebases

Dashboard & agents:
  attach         Open the dashboard (TUI) on the workspace daemon
  mcp            Run the MCP server (agent interface)
  features       List everything stems can do, by area, with commands, config keys and docs
  docs           List the documentation pages, or print one

Maintenance:
  daemon         Manage the workspace daemon
  upgrade        Upgrade stems (delegates to Homebrew when installed with brew)
  completions    Print a shell completion script
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
          current directory)

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

      --no-color
          Disable colours in human output
          
          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -q, --quiet
          Print only errors in human mode

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
          
          [env: STEMS_HOME]

  -V, --version
          Print version information (`--json` adds commit and build date)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Where to look:
  stems features [<area>]   everything stems can do, by area, with commands, config keys
                            and docs (`--json` for agents; docs/features.md)
  stems docs [<topic>]      list the reference pages, or print one
  stems <command> --help    the details; ends with related commands and docs

Lifecycle hooks (fixed `scripts:` names stems runs itself): setup, pre_start, start, health,
post_start, seed, pre_stop, stop, post_stop, build, reset; workspace: bootstrap, teardown.
Any other script name is a custom script (`stems run`). `stems scripts --lifecycle`
lists every hook with when it runs and who defines it.
```

### `stems init`

```text
Scaffold a new integration repo in the current (or --workspace) directory.

Creates stems.yaml (with a `yaml-language-server` schema reference), .gitignore, scripts/, env/ and
overlays/. Refuses to overwrite an existing stems.yaml (ALREADY_INITIALISED) unless --force.

Usage: stems init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --name <NAME>
          Workspace name (default: the directory name)

      --from <FROM>
          Start from an example workspace instead of an empty template

          Possible values:
          - minimal:    One process stem, no Docker
          - hello-shop: The full example: docker, compose, process and external stems

      --force
          Overwrite an existing stems.yaml

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
          current directory)

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

      --no-color
          Disable colours in human output
          
          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -q, --quiet
          Print only errors in human mode

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
          
          [env: STEMS_HOME]

See also: `stems validate`; docs/getting-started.md#1-create-an-integration-repo; `stems features
config`.
```

### `stems show`

```text
Print the resolved workspace config (or one stem's).

The resolved model after merging stems.local.yaml, includes and extends, applying defaults and
substituting `${…}` (every field is present; disabled stems are listed with `enabled: false`). With
a stem name, `data` is that stem. `--effective` adds `defaults`: the table of default values applied
to unset fields.

Usage: stems show [OPTIONS] [STEM]

Arguments:
  [STEM]
          Only this stem

Options:
      --effective
          Also print the table of defaults applied to unset fields

      --variant <NAME>
          Resolve the stem with this variant (or `local` for the base) active instead of the
          selected one. Nothing is written: `stems switch` changes the selection. Needs a stem

      --reveal
          Show secret env values instead of `<redacted>` (human output on a terminal only; refused
          with `--json`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
          current directory)

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

      --no-color
          Disable colours in human output
          
          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -q, --quiet
          Print only errors in human mode

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
          
          [env: STEMS_HOME]

See also: `stems env`, `stems logs`, `stems up`, `stems status`, `stems switch`; docs/config.md,
docs/config.md#include--extends-fr-ws-9, docs/config.md#secrets; `stems features config`.
```

### `stems up`

```text
Start stems (and their dependencies), attached or detached

Usage: stems up [OPTIONS] [STEMS]...

Arguments:
  [STEMS]...
          Stems to start (default: the profile's stems, or all)

Options:
      --profile <PROFILE>
          Profile to start

  -d, --detach
          Return once stems are up instead of staying attached

      --fresh
          Ignore stamps: run reset, setup and seed again

      --timeout <DURATION>
          Overall deadline (e.g. 90s)

      --fail-fast
          Stop starting further stems after the first failure (the default)

      --no-fail-fast
          Keep starting stems that do not depend on a failed one

      --max-parallel <N>
          Stems starting concurrently
          
          [default: 4]

      --pass-env <VAR>
          Pass these variables of the current shell to every stem (applied last; repeat or
          comma-separate)

      --no-watch
          Do not start watchdogs

      --build
          Rebuild compose services' images (`compose up --build`; the config's `build:`, default
          true, decides otherwise)

      --no-build
          Do not rebuild compose services' images for this run

      --sync
          Fetch git codebases before starting

      --force-overlays
          Back up conflicting overlay destinations and proceed

      --adopt-orphans
          Adopt orphaned processes that look like their stem's start command

      --kill-orphans
          Kill orphaned processes that look like their stem's start command

      --kill-foreign
          Also kill processes stems did not start that hold declared ports

  -y, --yes
          Answer yes to the orphan prompt (same as --kill-orphans)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
          current directory)

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

      --no-color
          Disable colours in human output
          
          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -q, --quiet
          Print only errors in human mode

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
          
          [env: STEMS_HOME]

See also: `stems down`, `stems start`, `stems stop`, `stems restart`, `stems show`;
docs/lifecycle.md#commands, docs/getting-started.md#4-add-your-services, docs/recovery.md; `stems
features lifecycle`.
```

### `stems restart`

```text
Restart stems (stop, then start)

Usage: stems restart [OPTIONS] <STEMS>...

Arguments:
  <STEMS>...
          Stems to restart

Options:
      --no-deps
          Do not start unstarted dependencies

      --build
          Re-run the `build` script first, and rebuild compose services' images (`compose up
          --build`)

      --no-build
          Do not rebuild compose services' images for this run (the config's `build:`, default true,
          decides otherwise)

      --timeout <DURATION>
          Deadline (e.g. 60s)

      --cascade
          Then restart their running hard dependants too, transitively, in dependency order
          (overrides `restart.cascade`; see docs/restart.md)

      --no-cascade
          Restart only these stems, even if `restart.cascade` is set

      --pass-env <VAR>
          Pass these variables of the current shell to the stems (applied last; repeat or
          comma-separate). Replaces the set they were started with; without it they keep that set

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
          current directory)

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

      --no-color
          Disable colours in human output
          
          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -q, --quiet
          Print only errors in human mode

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
          
          [env: STEMS_HOME]

See also: `stems build`, `stems status`, `stems up`, `stems down`, `stems start`;
docs/restart.md#cascading-restarts-fr-lc-9, docs/scripts.md#build-in-the-start-sequence-when,
docs/restart.md#policies; `stems features lifecycle`.
```

### `stems attach`

```text
Open the dashboard (TUI) on the workspace daemon.

Keys: j/k move, Enter detail, Tab cycles views, / filter, s sort, ? help, q quit (leaves the stems
running). STEMS_TUI=0, a non-terminal stdout or --json give the plain event stream instead.
--headless --script 'wait:healthy;frame;j;Enter;frame' replays keys and prints each frame as text
(see docs/tui.md).

Usage: stems attach [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --view <VIEW>
          Initial view

          Possible values:
          - table:  The stem table
          - detail: The selected stem's detail pane
          - graph:  The dependency graph

      --headless
          Render frames as text without a terminal (for tests)

      --script <SPEC>
          Key script to replay (implies --headless): tokens separated by `;`
          (`wait:healthy;frame;j;Enter;frame`), or `@FILE` to read them from a file

      --frames-out <DIR>
          Write rendered frames into this directory (with --headless)

      --size <WxH>
          Frame size with --headless (default 80x24)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
          current directory)

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

      --no-color
          Disable colours in human output
          
          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -q, --quiet
          Print only errors in human mode

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
          
          [env: STEMS_HOME]

See also: `stems up`; docs/tui.md; `stems features observe`.
```

### `stems status`

```text
Show the state of every stem.

Prints the table STEM TYPE STATUS REASON PID PORTS UPTIME RESTARTS (STATUS is a glyph and the state:
✓ healthy, ! degraded, ✗ failed, · stopped, ? unknown, ↻ transitioning; ASCII OK/WARN/FAIL/-/?/..
with --no-color, STEMS_ASCII=1 or a non-UTF-8 locale) and a summary line. --json gives `{stems,
summary}`. --watch redraws every INTERVAL until Ctrl-C (NDJSON frames with --json).

Usage: stems status [OPTIONS] [STEMS]...

Arguments:
  [STEMS]...
          Only these stems

Options:
      --enabled
          Hide disabled stems (`enabled: false`; listed last otherwise)

      --watch [<INTERVAL>]
          Redraw until Ctrl-C, every INTERVAL (seconds or a duration such as `500ms`; default 1s)

      --expect <STATE>
          Exit 0 when every named (else every enabled) stem is in STATE, else 1 (`STATUS_MISMATCH`,
          `data.mismatch: [{stem, state}]`). `stopped` accepts `failed` too; `running` is setup,
          starting, seeding, healthy or unhealthy. Without a daemon every stem is stopped

          Possible values:
          - healthy: Health check passing
          - stopped: Not running (`stopped`, `failed` or `disabled`)
          - failed:  Exited or could not be started
          - running: Up or on its way: `setup`, `starting`, `seeding`, `healthy` or `unhealthy`

      --timeout <DURATION>
          With --expect: keep checking (every 200 ms) until this long has passed (e.g. `30s`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
          current directory)

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

      --no-color
          Disable colours in human output
          
          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -q, --quiet
          Print only errors in human mode

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
          
          [env: STEMS_HOME]

See also: `stems show`, `stems restart`, `stems health`; docs/config.md#enabled,
docs/scripts.md#partial-installs-soft_fail,
docs/lifecycle.md#checking-states-in-scripts-status---expect; `stems features lifecycle`.
```

### `stems logs`

```text
Show or follow stem and script logs.

Prints captured lines (at most 10 000, the newest), several stems interleaved by time; with -f
replays the last 10 lines (or --since / --tail) and keeps streaming until Ctrl-C or the daemon
stops. With --json the output is NDJSON, one record per line (`{ts, stem, stream, tag, level, text,
fields}`) and no envelope. --export writes a .tar.gz bundle (status, events, redacted config, log
files) instead.

Usage: stems logs [OPTIONS] [STEMS]...

Arguments:
  [STEMS]...
          Only these stems

Options:
  -f, --follow
          Keep streaming new lines

      --since <SINCE>
          Start at this age or timestamp (e.g. 10m)

      --until <UNTIL>
          Stop at this age or timestamp

      --grep <REGEX>
          Only lines matching this regex

      --level <LEVEL>
          Level filter: `error` (exactly that level) or `warn+` (warn and above)

      --script <NAME>
          Only output of this script (lines tagged with its name)

      --tail <N>
          Last N lines

      --export
          Write a log bundle (.tar.gz) instead of printing

  -o, --output <FILE>
          Output file for --export

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
```

```text

(`{ts, seq, kind, stem, from, to, reason, actor, data}`) and no envelope: the hook for external
automation. Errors still use the envelope (e.g. exit 4 DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING).

Usage: stems events [OPTIONS]

Options:
```

### `stems metrics`

```text
Show CPU, memory and disk usage per stem.

The table has STEM CPU% MEM CHILDREN UPTIME RESTARTS and CPU/MEM sparklines over the last 30
samples, plus a TOTAL row. CPU% is percent of one core (can exceed 100); MEM is resident memory of
the whole process tree (containers: usage minus cache). `--sort cpu|mem` puts the heaviest first
("what is eating my laptop"); `--history 5m` adds the samples of that window to --json; `--disk`
also measures build outputs (target, dist, build, node_modules, .venv) and docker volumes (slow,
cached 60 s). --json gives `{interval_ms, stems: [{name, type, state, latest: {ts, cpu_pct,
rss_bytes, children, uptime_s, restarts}, history?, open_ports, limits, disk?}], totals: {cpu_pct,
rss_bytes, children}}`. See docs/metrics.md.

Usage: stems metrics [OPTIONS] [STEMS]...

Options:

      --history <DURATION>
          Include samples from this window (e.g. 5m)

      --sort <SORT>
          Sort order

          Possible values:
```

### `stems run`

```text
Run a stem or workspace script.

`stems run <stem> <script> [-- args…]` runs a stem's script; `stems run --ws <script> [-- args…]` a
workspace-level script (`--workspace-script` is an alias; `--workspace` stays the global flag that
selects the workspace). Arguments after `--` are validated against the script's `args` schema
(`SCRIPT_ARGS_INVALID`, exit 2) and passed as `--name value` flags plus `STEMS_ARG_<NAME>` env;
scripts without a schema get them untouched. Exit 0 when the script succeeded, else 1
(`SCRIPT_FAILED`). Lifecycle hooks (below) can be run by name too. See docs/scripts.md.

Usage: stems run [OPTIONS] [STEM] [SCRIPT] [-- <ARGS>...]

Arguments:
  [STEM]
          Stem whose script to run

  [SCRIPT]
          Script name

  [ARGS]...
          Script arguments (after `--`), e.g. `-- --email a@b.c`

Options:
      --ws <SCRIPT>
          Run a workspace-level script instead of a stem script (`--workspace-script` is an alias)

      --start-deps
          Start the script's `requires:` stems if they are not healthy

      --stop-deps
          Stop the script's `requires_stopped:` stems if they run

      --wait <DURATION>
          How long to wait for the stem while it is still starting (default 30s)

      --no-wait
          Return the run id at once instead of waiting for the script to finish (follow it with
          `stems events -f`)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
          current directory)

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

      --no-color
          Disable colours in human output
          
          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -q, --quiet
          Print only errors in human mode

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
          
          [env: STEMS_HOME]

Lifecycle hooks, in lifecycle order (every other `scripts:` name is a custom script):
  bootstrap   (workspace) once per `up`, before any stem starts
  setup       before the first start, again when its stamp (inputs, stamp_env) changes
  pre_start   before every start of the process, policy restarts included
  start       the process itself (instead of `command`); `starting` until the health check passes
  health      reserved for the `health: {type: command}` probe's output; never a custom script
  post_start  after every start, once the stem is healthy
  seed        after post_start, once; again when its stamp changes (state `seeding`)
  pre_stop    before every stop, before the process is signalled
  stop        how to stop the process (instead of SIGTERM), bounded by `stop_grace`
  post_stop   after every stop, once the process is gone
  build       on `stems build` and `restart --build` (between stop and start); with `when:
  changed|always` also in every start, after `setup`
  reset       on `stems reset` and `up --fresh`, after the stop; its stamps are cleared
  teardown    (workspace) on `down --all`, after every stem stopped, before the daemon exits
`stems scripts --lifecycle` prints this table with the stems that define each hook.

See also: `stems scripts`; docs/scripts.md#custom-scripts-and-stems-run,
docs/scripts.md#the-lifecycle-order; `stems features scripts`.
```

```text
Lifecycle hooks, in lifecycle order (every other `scripts:` name is a custom script):

  pre_start   before every start of the process, policy restarts included
```

### `stems exec`

```text
Run an ad-hoc command in a stem's context (env, cwd or container).

A process or external stem: the command runs here, in your terminal, with your environment plus what
stems sets for the stem (`PORT`, `env`, `env_files`, `STEMS_*`, dependencies' ports and outputs), in
its codebase (else its state directory). A running docker/compose stem: `docker exec` into its
container (`--host` runs on the host instead). The exit code is the command's. Works without a
daemon (from the config; auto ports then stay unresolved) and never starts one. `--json` prints
`{stem, container, cwd, argv, exit}` after the command (its output still streams first). See
docs/exec.md.

Usage: stems exec [OPTIONS] <STEM> -- <COMMAND>...

Arguments:

          Stem whose context to use

  <COMMAND>...
          Command and arguments (after `--`)

Options:

          Run on the host even for a docker/compose stem

      --cwd <DIR>
          Working directory (default: the stem's codebase, else its state directory). Host only

      --fresh
          Keep only PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, TMPDIR, TERM, LANG and LC_* of your
          environment (like a script's `inherit_env: false`). Host only

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
          current directory)

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

      --no-color
          Disable colours in human output
          
          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -q, --quiet
          Print only errors in human mode

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
          
          [env: STEMS_HOME]

See also: `stems shell`, `stems env`; docs/exec.md; `stems features env`.
```

### `stems repos sync`

```text
Clone missing git codebases and fetch/check out their refs.

A tree with local work (uncommitted changes, unpushed commits, or HEAD moved by you, e.g. with
`repos checkout`) is left alone (`skipped_dirty`); `--reset` returns a moved tree to the declared
ref (local work is still never touched).

Arguments:

Options:
      --recurse-submodules
```

### `stems repos checkout`

```text
Check out any branch, tag or sha of a stem's git codebase.

Fetches, then checks out the ref detached (a branch as `origin/<branch>`). Refuses uncommitted
changes (`REPO_DIRTY`) unless `--force`, which carries them over like `git checkout`. Nothing is
recorded: `repos status` shows `drift: true`, `repos sync` leaves the tree alone, `repos sync
--reset <stem>` goes back to the declared ref.

Usage: stems repos checkout [OPTIONS] <STEM> <REF>

Arguments:
  <STEM>
          Stem whose git codebase to move

  <REF>
          Branch, tag or sha

Options:
      --force
          Check out even with uncommitted changes (they are carried over) or with commits on HEAD
          that no remote branch or tag has (they stay reachable from the reflog only)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
          current directory)

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

      --no-color
          Disable colours in human output
          
          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -q, --quiet
          Print only errors in human mode

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
          
          [env: STEMS_HOME]

See also: docs/repos.md; `stems features repos`.
```

### `stems env`

```text
Print the environment stems gives a stem.

What stems sets (`PORT`, `env`, `env_files`, local env, `STEMS_*`, dependencies' ports and outputs)
as dotenv `KEY=value` lines; `--format shell` prints `export KEY='value'` (`eval "$(stems env api
--format shell)"`), `--format json` / `--json` gives `data: {stem, env, cwd, container,
unresolved}`. `--all` adds your own environment underneath. Secret outputs are redacted. Works
without a daemon (never starts one). See docs/exec.md.

Arguments:

          The stem

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:

          - shell:  `export KEY='value'` lines, for `eval`
          - json:   The JSON envelope
          
          [default: dotenv]

      --all

      --reveal
          Show secret values (human output on a terminal only)

  -h, --help

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
```

### `stems daemon stop`

```text
Stop the workspace daemon.

Asks it to shut down (the same orderly path as SIGTERM: every running stem is stopped first) and
waits for its socket and lock to disappear: as long as the daemon's shutdown budget
(`daemon.shutdown_timeout`, by default derived from the running stems' stop graces; the `shutdown`
reply carries it) plus 5 s, unless `--timeout` or `--no-wait`. A daemon still stopping when the wait
ends is DAEMON_STILL_STOPPING (exit 1; it keeps stopping, run the command again to keep waiting).
Exits 4 (DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING) when none is running; a stale lock left by a crashed daemon is removed.

Usage: stems daemon stop [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --timeout <DURATION>
          How long to wait for the daemon to exit (e.g. 120s) instead of its shutdown budget plus 5
          s

      --no-wait
          Return as soon as the daemon accepted the shutdown (`data.stopping: true`); it keeps
          stopping in the background

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global options:
      --workspace <PATH>
          Workspace directory or stems.yaml path (default: $STEMS_WORKSPACE, else walk up from the
          current directory)

      --json
          Emit the JSON envelope (the default when stdout is not a terminal)

      --human
          Emit human text even when stdout is not a terminal

      --no-color
          Disable colours in human output
          
          [env: STEMS_NO_COLOR]

  -q, --quiet
          Print only errors in human mode

  -v, --verbose...
          More detail (repeat for more: -vv)

      --home <PATH>
          Root for daemon state, sockets, locks and logs (default: ~/Library/Application
          Support/stems on macOS, $XDG_STATE_HOME/stems or ~/.local/state/stems on Linux)
          
          [env: STEMS_HOME]

See also: `stems daemon start`, `stems daemon status`; docs/protocol.md; `stems features agents`.
```
